title: Socket and wire ownership boundary
summary: NORM is a SocketProvider implementation engine, not an application semantic protocol.
invariants: Applications use SocketAddressProvider, SocketSelector and SocketProvider; they do not call NormCreateSession, NormStartReceiver, NormSetSSM or IP multicast membership APIs directly.
The full NORM SocketAddress survives above the provider boundary with group, port, interface, optional source filter and node identity; it is not flattened to host:port.
libnorm owns NORM sessions, NACK/FEC, congestion and UDP/IP multicast mechanics; the native ooRexx binding owns native handle and enqueue-buffer lifetime.
The application-visible call stays stable when another qualified provider such as XTP is selected for the same semantic request.
